title: Notes with Headings

illustrates.quote: Do not insert a blank line between a note separation line and a title or heading. (See Sample 16-2: Notes with Headings on page 16-18.)

blocks.text: I like a look of Agony
blocks.features: Poem title in large display type, with byline 'Emily Dickinson' beneath it in bold.

blocks.text:
I like a look of Agony, Because I know it's true— Men do not sham [ref:3]Convulsion, Nor simulate, a [ref:4]Throe—
The Eyes glaze once—and that is Death— Impossible to feign The Beads upon the Forehead By homely Anguish strung.
blocks.features: Poem set with print line number '5' beside its fifth line; two words ('Convulsion', 'Throe') carry superscript numeral reference marks keyed to notes at the right.

blocks.text:
[ref:3] sham Convulsion: pretend to have a seizure.
[ref:4] Throe: sudden surge of pain.
blocks.features: Two short glossary notes at the right margin of the first poem.

blocks.text: “Good Night, Willie Lee, I'll See You in the Morning”
blocks.features: Second poem title in large display type, with byline 'Alice Walker' beneath it in bold.

blocks.text: Looking down into my father's dead face for the last time my mother said without tears, without smiles without regrets but with [ref:1]civility “Good night, Willie Lee, I'll see you in the morning.”
blocks.features: Left column of the second poem, with print line number '5' at its fifth line; the word 'civility' carries a superscript numeral note reference.

blocks.text: And it was then I knew that the healing of all our wounds is forgiveness that permits a promise of our return at the end.
blocks.features: Right column of the second poem, with print line number '10' at its first line.

blocks.text: [ref:1] civility: politeness, especially of a merely formal kind.
blocks.features: Single glossary note below a short rule at the foot of the second poem's right column.

notes.text: sham Convulsion: pretend to have a seizure.
civility: politeness, especially of a merely formal kind.

print.surroundingText: Cross-referenced from rule 16.5.1h, illustrating cell-5 poem-title headings immediately following note separation lines with no intervening blank line, when multiple titled passages with their own notes share one print page.
print.printFeatures: Two poem excerpts on decorative colored backgrounds, each with its own title/byline heading and numbered notes; print page number '268' at the foot.

pageBreaks.note: Explicit —New Braille Page— marker in the source, after braille line 23 (print line 23, the last line before the marker); the line-number field (2-digit, width 5) restarts at 1 on the new page.

braille.notes: Line-number field width 5 (digits up to 2, +3) used throughout both braille pages of this sample, per source. The cell-5 heading titles ('I like a look of Agony', the byline, and the second poem's title/byline) each sit directly after either the sample's own opening or a note separation line, with no intervening blank line, per rule 16.5.1h. Blank-cell-only lines are recorded as empty strings.

resolution: illustrates.rule set to 16.5.1.h per standards-map.md's own BANA §16/B004 §11 worked-examples table (the project's established canonical id), not either run's own guess. print.blocks/print.notes follow Run B's schema ([ref:MARK] tokens inline + a separate print.notes[] array of {ref, placement, text}), matching this task's required schema; Run A instead folded each note's real content directly into a sibling print.blocks entry with no [ref:MARK] markers and always an empty print.notes[] -- a schema-level difference, not a content disagreement. braille.width: verified directly: line 12918 (field width 5, digits(23)+3), after stripping a leading form-feed page-break character and the line-number field, is exactly 40 characters, right-justified to '#bfh'; line 12942 (the note-separation line on the second braille page) is also exactly 40. braille.lines: the two runs' transcriptions disagreed on leading blank-cell counts / an inserted anomalous token on specific lines; resolved by direct re-extraction from references/_text/braille-formats-2016.txt (U+2800 cells converted to spaces, fixed padding measured exactly) -- see differences.md for the line-by-line count.
